items.title: Week 2 practice assessment
prompts: Given specified sets, use unions and intersections to determine what the topology axioms force to be open.
Use inverse images of open sets to justify continuity of $f(x)=2x$.

items.title: Week 3 assessment
prompts: Show that $f^{-1}(U\cap V)=f^{-1}(U)\cap f^{-1}(V)$ and explain how this is used in reasoning about continuity.
Do intervals with integer endpoints form a basis for the usual topology on $\mathbb R$? Justify your answer.

items.title: Week 4 assessment
prompts: Let $X$ be a topological space. State what it means for a collection $\mathcal B$ of open subsets of $X$ to be a basis for the topology on $X$.
Let $\mathcal B$ be a basis for $X$, and let $A\subseteq X$ have the subspace topology. Prove that $\mathcal B_A=\{B\cap A:B\in\mathcal B\}$ is a basis for the subspace topology on $A$.

items.title: Week 5 assessment
prompts: Let $q:X\to Y$ be a surjective map, where $X$ is a topological space. State the definition of the quotient topology on $Y$.
Let $q:X\to Y$ be a quotient map and $g:Y\to Z$ a function. Suppose $g\circ q:X\to Z$ is continuous. Prove that $g$ is continuous.

items.title: Week 6 assessment
prompts: Let $A\subseteq X$. Define the closure $\overline A$ and state what $x\in\overline A$ means in terms of neighborhoods of $x$.
Let $f:X\to Y$ be continuous and let $A\subseteq X$. Prove that $f(\overline A)\subseteq\overline{f(A)}$. In words: the image of the closure of $A$ is contained in the closure of the image of $A$.
